text:
emma-cs: FYI - AcmeHealth is hitting 503s on hosted inference since ~08:20Z. They report 'upstream handler crashed' and saw sudden billing spike. Impacting redwood-3b-quant and some toolcalls.

infra-bot: [alert] 08:21:05 upstream-runner exited (signal 6) x7 on host gpu-wn-42. 503s spike detected for route /v1/generate from acmehealth-org.

sanjay-eng-runtime: I'm pulling logs now. Initial glance: container crashed during an NVML MIG transition. nvml error around the time of the backtrace.

sanjay-eng-runtime: log snippet:
```
2024-04-01 08:20:59 infer-runner[pid=1243]: runtime: fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT)
Backtrace: ...
[ 1120.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1120.345689] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00: failed MIG transition: -22
nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses // error -4
```

maria-eng-sre: Confirming: the host attempted a MIG reconfigure (driver initiated) while infer-runner was live. That aligns with the SIGABRT. Can we confirm whether any scheduled maintenance or autoscaler actions triggered MIG ops?

alex-mlops: We had a model hot-swap on that host (hotmodel rollout) at 08:20 as part of the rolling canary for quant profile changes. The orchestration might have touched GPU instance config to optimize packing.

oncall: Triage plan: 1) Quick mitigation - route AcmeHealth to fallback pool (cpu/dedicated-small) 2) Cordon hosts with recent MIG ops 3) Disable automated MIG transitions in runtime 4) Collect full coredump and nvml logs.

noah-support: Noted — I've told AcmeHealth we are investigating and offered to temporarily move them to a dedicated pool; they accepted fallback routing. Also offered billing credit for the window.

maria-eng-sre: Executing mitigation commands now:
```
# cordon nodes showing mig-change=true
kubectl label node gpu-wn-42 temporary-mig-disabled=true && kubectl drain gpu-wn-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# add routing override for customer
redwoodctl routes create --org acmehealth --policy fallback_pool:dedicated-gpu-fallback
```

deploy-bot: rollout aborted for quant-hot-swap job id=qc-3912 at 08:22. Canary instances removed from gpu-wn-42.

sanjay-eng-runtime: Repro notes: I repro'd locally by doing a MIG create/destroy while infer-runner has ongoing KV-cache allocations and streaming contexts. The runtime path that handles hot MIG returns an unexpected errno and we hit an unchecked assert leading to SIGABRT.

sanjay-eng-runtime: Minimal repro steps I used:
1) start infer-runner with a longstream job (pinned context)
2) `nvidia-smi mig -cgi` create a MIG instance on the same GPU
3) trigger model swap (hotload)
4) observe process SIGABRT within ~1-2s

alex-mlops: Workaround for now: disable hotmodel MIG-aware packing for hosted; force model swap to use live-compat variant (no MIG reconfigure). We'll flip the canary gating.

maria-eng-sre: We've collected dmesg + nvml + core. Uploading to /s3/triage/1702468019-acme-mig-core.tar.gz and added to incident ticket #INC-2931.

oncall: Short-term action items:
- (P0) Keep AcmeHealth on fallback pool until patch.
- (P0) Prevent any more automated MIG transitions for hosted hosts.
- (P1) Revert driver update on a small canary set if needed.
- (P1) Add proper errno handling in runtime MIG path.

noah-support: CS notes: Customer wants ETA for fix + confirmation that their data wasn't exposed. We told them there is no evidence of data leak; this is an infra-level process crash. Offering 24h credits.

sanjay-eng-runtime: Root cause hypothesis: runtime tries to call nvml->reconfigure while GPU is handling process list queries; nvml returns EINVAL / -22 during MIG change on some driver versions which our code interprets poorly. Unchecked precondition -> abort().

maria-eng-sre: Repro on driver 525.85 shows failure; driver 525.78 on a canary host did not reproduce under same steps. I'll schedule a narrow driver rollback test.

oncall: Can someone attach the exact error string that hit the API gateway? CS needs verbatim for their ticket.

sanjay-eng-runtime: API gateway saw upstream error: "upstream: handler exited with status 134 (SIGABRT) -- upstream service unreachable". 503s returned to client.

noah-support: Sent that to AcmeHealth with the mitigation steps and SRE contact. They asked for a postmortem and credits.

alex-mlops: Timeline for dev fix: 24-48h to add errno checks + graceful fallback to keep process alive when MIG reconfig returns recoverable errors. If driver rollback mitigates, we may push shorter perf-safe hotfix.

maria-eng-sre: Next: schedule a controlled test with driver rollback on 2 hosts at 10:00Z. If green, we'll roll to affected fleet and re-enable canaries slowly.

oncall: I'll keep this thread updated. If you see additional 500/503 spikes, ping with tag @oncall immediately. :rotating_light:

emma-cs: Thanks all — CS will follow up with customer and log billing request. Please add postmortem link when available. :thumbsup:

maria-eng-sre: Incident record created INC-2931. Adding notes and upload links. Will produce postmortem after root cause and fix.

deploy-bot: migration of acmehealth route -> dedicated-gpu-fallback completed at 08:29.

oncall: last check: error rate for AcmeHealth reduced to baseline after reroute. Marking mitigated. Will keep P0 until code patch is merged.

maria-eng-sre: (action) Raise follow-up to runtime team to add unit test covering MIG failure path and to CI GPU smoke tests.

emma-cs: Acknowledged. Closing customer alert for now; will reopen if they report further issues.
